headline: FCC issues its first bans on gadgets under new foreign-chip rule
summary: Using a power it gave itself on October 13th to block gadgets containing chips from companies on its national-security threat list, the FCC issued its first bans: a HiSilicon dashcam and wireless video transmitter, which the agency says contain "foreign surveillance chips" including an AI chip with face-detection algorithms.

claims.statement: On October 13th the FCC gave itself a new power to block gadgets containing a chip from any company on its national-security threat list.

sources.quote: On October 13th, Brendan Carr's FCC gave itself a new power - it can block gadgets for containing any computer chip made by any company on its list of potential threats to national security.

claims.statement: The FCC used that power for the first time, blocking two gadgets it says contain "foreign surveillance chips."

sources.quote: Today, it's exercising that power for the first time, blocking two gadgets because they contain "foreign surveillance chips," the FCC claims.

claims.statement: The banned devices are a dashcam and wireless video transmitter made by HiSilicon, a Huawei subsidiary, over an AI chip that advertises face-detection algorithms.

sources.quote: FCC bans a dashcam and wireless video transmitter produced by HiSilicon, a subsidiary of Huawei for containing an AI chip that advertises face detection algorithms.
